title: Data Security: Handling and Encryption

header.html: 5.1 Understand data security: Data handling (for example classification, labeling, masking, and sanitization); Encryption (for example symmetric, asymmetric, hashing, quantum resistant cryptography)
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

toc.title: The data life cycle and handling

html:
1Data classification and labeling

Classification sorts data by sensitivity, so each level gets matching protection. Labeling marks the data (file, email, document) with its level so people and systems treat it correctly.

Typical level Meaning Example
Public No harm if disclosed Press release
Internal (private) For staff only Internal memo
Confidential (sensitive) Serious harm if disclosed Customer records, contracts
Restricted (secret) Severe harm if disclosed Trade secrets, health data

The data owner decides the classification; the custodian runs the protection. Classification drives access, encryption and retention.

Exam tip

. The data owner classifies; the custodian protects. Unlabeled data is hard to protect: label it.

2The data life cycle and handling

Stage Security action
Create or collect Classify and collect only what is needed (minimization)
Store Encrypt, control access, back up
Use Least privilege, monitoring
Share Approved channels only, encryption, data loss prevention
Archive Retain as law and policy require
Destroy Sanitize so data cannot be recovered

Data states: at rest (stored), in transit (moving), in use (being processed). Encrypt at rest and in transit.

AI workspaces: staff must not paste confidential data into public AI tools because of data leakage; classify and mask data first.

3Masking and sanitization

Technique What it does
Masking Hides part of a value (a card shown as XXXX1234); the original stays in the source
Tokenization Replaces a value with a random token; the real value is stored elsewhere
Sanitization Removes data from media so it cannot be recovered
Sanitization method Meaning
Clear Overwrite the data; fine for reuse inside the organization
Purge Stronger methods (degauss, cryptographic erase); media may be reused
Destroy Physical destruction (shred, incinerate); highest assurance
Exam tip

. Deleting a file is not sanitizing. Destroy for the highest assurance. Cryptographic erase means destroying the key.

4Encryption basics

Encryption turns plaintext into ciphertext with an algorithm and a key. It protects confidentiality.

Type Keys Speed Use
Symmetric (for example AES) One shared key Fast Bulk data, disks, VPN traffic
Asymmetric (for example RSA, ECC) Key pair: public and private Slower Key exchange, digital signatures
Hashing (for example SHA-256) No key; one-way Fast Integrity, password storage (with salt)
Rule Fact
Encrypt with the receiver's public key; only the private key decrypts Confidentiality with asymmetric keys
Sign with your private key; anyone verifies with your public key Authenticity and non-repudiation
Hash cannot be reversed; the same input always gives the same hash Integrity check
Key management Protect, rotate and back up keys; a lost key means lost data

Public key infrastructure (PKI) uses certificates issued by a certificate authority to bind a public key to an identity. TLS protects data in transit on the web.

Quantum-resistant (post-quantum) cryptography means algorithms designed to withstand quantum computers, which could break RSA and ECC. Organizations plan to move to them.

Exam tip

. Symmetric = one key, fast. Asymmetric = key pair, slower. Hash = no key, one way. Hashing is not encryption.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Who decides the classification level of a set of customer records?

  • AThe network administrator who stores the data
  • BThe external auditor who reviews the data
  • CThe data owner, who is accountable for the data
  • DThe software vendor who sold the system
Show the answer

Answer: C. The data owner decides the classification; the custodian applies the protection.

S2Which technology is best for encrypting a large database quickly?

  • ASymmetric encryption such as AES
  • BHashing with SHA-256
  • CA digital signature with a private key
  • DAsymmetric encryption such as RSA
Show the answer

Answer: A. Symmetric encryption is fast and suits bulk data.

S3A user wants to prove that a file was not changed during download. What should be compared?

  • AThe hash value of the file
  • BThe public key of the sender
  • CThe encryption key of the file
  • DThe classification label of the file
Show the answer

Answer: A. A hash gives an integrity check: if the hash is the same, the file is unchanged.

S4A hard disk with sensitive data is retired and the data must be impossible to recover. Which method gives the highest assurance?

  • ADeleting the files and emptying the recycle bin
  • BPhysically destroying the disk
  • CFormatting the disk with a quick format
  • DOverwriting the disk once with zeros
Show the answer

Answer: B. Physical destruction gives the highest assurance of sanitization.

S5A customer service tool shows only the last four digits of a card number. What technique is this?

  • AHashing of the card number
  • BSymmetric encryption of the file
  • CCryptographic erase of the disk
  • DMasking of the sensitive value
Show the answer

Answer: D. Showing only part of a value hides the rest from the viewer, which is masking.

S6Which risk makes organizations plan for quantum-resistant cryptography?

  • AQuantum computers may slow down symmetric ciphers
  • BQuantum computers may break RSA and ECC
  • CQuantum computers may lose hash values
  • DQuantum computers may block firewall ports
Show the answer

Answer: B. Quantum computers could break current asymmetric algorithms such as RSA and ECC.

5.2 Recall questions

R1How many keys does symmetric encryption use?

Show the answer

One shared key.

R2Which key decrypts a message encrypted with the receiver's public key?

Show the answer

The receiver's private key.

R3What does a digital signature use to sign?

Show the answer

The sender's private key.

R4Is hashing reversible?

Show the answer

No, it is one way.

R5What are the three data states?

Show the answer

At rest, in transit, in use.

R6What are the three sanitization methods?

Show the answer

Clear, purge, destroy.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Classification public, internal, confidential, restricted; owner decides, custodian protects
Data states at rest, in transit, in use; encrypt at rest and in transit
Masking / tokenization hide part of a value / replace with a token
Sanitization clear, purge, destroy; deleting is not sanitizing
Encryption symmetric one key; asymmetric key pair; hash one way
Signatures sign with private key, verify with public key
Quantum plan quantum-resistant algorithms
